# ADR-064 — Checkpoint 9.5: Calendar is an authoring surface — explicit event ownership, durable outbound sync, whole-series recurrence (migration 0019)

**Status:** Locked

<!-- Decision text below is verbatim from the pre-split docs/DECISIONS.md table row (2026-09-16). Do not edit a Locked decision without explicit owner approval. -->

**Checkpoint 9.5 — Calendar is an authoring surface: explicit event ownership, durable outbound sync, whole-series recurrence, no new consent (2026-09-14, owner-directed).** One migration, `0019_event_authoring` (`events.origin text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'external'` + CHECK, `events.client_uuid text` + partial unique index, `calendar_connection_calendars.access_role text`; level **20**), justified as explicit ownership, idempotency and write-capability metadata — the three things the migration policy names. **1. OWNERSHIP IS A COLUMN, NOT AN INFERENCE.** Phase 4 built genuine two-way sync, and after the first push an imported event and an authored event were byte-identical in the database: the `event_external_links` row carried no direction, `external_source` was never written, and the link evaporated on archive. Measured consequence before 9.5: archiving an imported event deleted it from the owner's Google calendar, and editing one wrote back to a calendar whose writability was unknown. `origin='external'` is now READ-ONLY through `PATCH`, `/archive`, `/detach`, `/cancel-occurrence` and `/link-calendar` (`409 event_not_owned`); `origin='local'` is editable, cancellable and pushable. **The default is `external` on purpose**: all 98 production rows were sync-ingested, a backfill `UPDATE` is not reconcilable, and a writer that forgets the column fails SAFE (read-only) — every local writer sets `local` explicitly and a test pins each. The rollout window (migrate → recreate api → recreate worker) is the one place a genuinely authored row can be stamped `external`; the runbook checks `origin='external' AND no link AND created_at > migrate instant` after rollout. **2. WRITES ARE DURABLE INTENT.** `POST /events` with a `calendar` inserts event + occurrence window + `pending_push` link in one transaction; every later mutation flips the link to `pending_push` in-transaction; enqueue happens after commit and a lost enqueue is re-driven from the rows by the five-minute calendar cron. Under pg-boss `standard` policy `singletonKey` is inert (recorded, not relied on): duplicate pushes are tolerated because the push is idempotent. **3. PROVIDER IDEMPOTENCY BY DERIVED IDENTITY.** The Google event id is `link.id` without dashes (base32hex-legal) and is SENT on insert; `409 duplicate` falls through to an update. The CalDAV UID/href are derived the same way and `412` on `If-None-Match: *` means "exists". Inbound sync ADOPTS a pending link whose derived id matches an incoming remote event instead of importing a read-only twin — found by two independent reviewers as the one path that duplicated locally and then wedged the original on the unique index. Full-sync reconcile archives only links `synced` before the listing began. The final write is race-safe: ids unconditionally, `synced` only where the link's `updated_at` is unchanged since job start. **4. WRITE-ELIGIBILITY IS PROVIDER-REPORTED.** A Google calendar is a target only when `access_role in (owner, writer)`; NULL is unknown and never writable; CalDAV has no role and the PUT is the check. `access_role` is refreshed by the Settings listing, at the toggle-on insert, and by the worker's calendar cron, which also NULLs roles for calendars no longer listed. **Consent is unchanged**: the existing grant is `calendar.events` (read-write) — verified in the native authorization request and in production's stored scope — so no re-consent and no ADR-053a exposure. **5. RECURRENCE CROSSES THE BOUNDARY THROUGH ONE LAYER** (`localRecurrenceToGoogle` ↔ `googleRecurrenceToLocal`), round-trip-tested for every preset, UNTIL/COUNT, DST and EXDATE; the 9.4 task presets are reused minus the completion anchor; `validateEventRecurrenceRule` is shared by POST/PATCH and capture commit, so `hasCommittableRecurrence` now refuses an uncommittable event rule at confirm exactly as it does for tasks. Series editing is WHOLE-SERIES: "this event only" on a linked local series is refused (`409 linked_series_detach_unsupported`) because `events.insert` does not create a Google exception; cancelling one occurrence (EXDATE) is supported. Inbound all-day UNTIL resolves to end of local day in the master's zone (the pre-9.5 midnight resolution silently dropped the final instance of every imported all-day series with an UNTIL). **6. FAILURE SEMANTICS.** Transient → retry → dead letter → `calendar.push-event.dead:<eventId>:<link updated_at>` (ADR-058); permanent (`missing_scope`, `invalid_request`, `not_found`) → `error`, no retry, surfaced on the event screen; inactive connection → link stays `pending_push` so reconnecting resumes it. **Unchanged and reaffirmed:** ADR-018, ADR-042/045, ADR-053a (no scope change), ADR-058, ADR-063. **Recorded, not fixed:** no `If-Match` on Google update (inbound `decideConflict` is the guard); `singletonKey` inert; `recurrence_timezone ≠ timezone` only reachable by a raw API caller; a remote un-delete re-imports as a new external row; `BYMONTHDAY=-1` acceptance by Google is verified only at production acceptance (Checkpoint 9.5, 2026-09-14)
